meaning: In contact with someone by phone, message or letter.
japanese: 連絡を取り合っている。
cue: Ask a friend about old classmates.
reply: Are you still in touch with anyone from school?
replyJapanese: 学校時代の友達の誰かと、今も連絡を取っていますか。
transferCue: End a phone call with a customer who is waiting for a repair.
transferReply: I'll be in touch as soon as the parts arrive.
transferReplyJapanese: 部品が届きしだい、ご連絡します。
nuance: Touch takes no article, and the person follows with. Get in touch starts contact; keep or stay in touch continues it.
nuanceJapanese: touch に冠詞は付かず、相手は with で続ける。get in touch は連絡を始めること、keep / stay in touch は連絡を続けること。

meaning: Being used at the moment.
japanese: 使用中である。使われている。
cue: A colleague wants to book a meeting room.
reply: Room four is in use until three o'clock.
replyJapanese: 第4会議室は3時まで使用中です。
transferCue: Describe an old machine that still works.
transferReply: That photocopier has been in use for twenty years.
transferReplyJapanese: あのコピー機は20年間使われています。
nuance: Use is a noun here and takes no article. The opposite is out of use, for things that are broken or no longer used.
nuanceJapanese: この use は名詞で、冠詞は付かない。反対は out of use で、故障中のものや、もう使われていないものに言う。

meaning: Used to say that something should have happened earlier.
japanese: そろそろ〜してもいいころだ。やっとだ。
cue: Your flatmate's phone screen has been cracked for a year.
reply: It's about time you bought a new phone.
replyJapanese: そろそろ新しいスマホを買ってもいいころだよ。
transferCue: A colleague says the lift has finally been repaired.
transferReply: It's about time. We've been using the stairs since March.
transferReplyJapanese: やっとですね。3月からずっと階段を使っていましたから。
frame: It's about time someone did something
nuance: The verb after it is in the past tense although the meaning is present: it's about time you went. On its own, About time! shows mild annoyance at a delay.
nuanceJapanese: あとの動詞は過去形にするが、意味は現在のこと（it's about time you went）。単独の About time! は、遅れへの軽いいら立ちを表す。

meaning: Almost.
japanese: ほとんど。だいたい。
cue: A friend asks if dinner is ready.
reply: Dinner's just about ready, so please sit down.
replyJapanese: 夕食はもうほとんどできたので、座ってください。
transferCue: Describe how your colleagues travel to work.
transferReply: Just about everyone in the office cycles to work.
transferReplyJapanese: オフィスのほぼ全員が、自転車で通勤しています。
nuance: Informal, and it goes before the word it describes. In British English it can also mean only just, as in I can just about reach.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた言い方で、修飾する語の前に置く。イギリス英語では I can just about reach のように「かろうじて」の意味にもなる。

meaning: Give someone enough to do so that they are not bored.
japanese: （人を）退屈させないよう、することを与えておく。
cue: A neighbour asks how you are enjoying retirement.
reply: The garden keeps me busy for most of the summer.
replyJapanese: 夏のあいだはほとんど、庭の手入れで忙しくしています。
transferCue: Describe a long car journey with children.
transferReply: A bag of puzzles kept them busy for the whole drive.
transferReplyJapanese: パズルをひと袋持たせたら、あの子たちは道中ずっと退屈しませんでした。
nuance: The person goes between keep and busy. Without an object, keep busy means stay active yourself: I like to keep busy.
nuanceJapanese: 人は keep と busy の間に置く。目的語のない keep busy は「自分が忙しくしている」の意味（I like to keep busy）。

meaning: Record how many of something there are as the number changes.
japanese: 数を数えておく。回数を把握しておく。
cue: Guests are starting to arrive at an event you are helping with.
reply: Can you keep count of how many people come in?
replyJapanese: 入ってくる人数を数えておいてもらえますか。
transferCue: Talk about a friend's many trips to the same country.
transferReply: She's been to Italy so often that I've stopped keeping count.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はイタリアに何度も行っているので、もう数えるのをやめました。
nuance: No article before count, and the thing counted follows of. The opposite is lose count.
nuanceJapanese: count に冠詞は付かず、数える対象は of で続ける。反対は lose count（数がわからなくなる）。

meaning: Used to tell someone to continue doing something well.
japanese: その調子で続けて。
cue: A new colleague has had a strong first month.
reply: Your reports are really clear, so keep it up.
replyJapanese: 報告書がとてもわかりやすいです。その調子で続けてください。
transferCue: Your friend has been training three times a week.
transferReply: If you keep it up, you'll be ready for the race by May.
transferReplyJapanese: この調子で続ければ、5月にはレースに出られるよ。
nuance: It points back to the effort just mentioned and does not change to them. Keep up the good work means the same.
nuanceJapanese: it は直前に話題にした努力を指し、them などには変えない。Keep up the good work も同じ意味。

meaning: Say nothing about something.
japanese: 黙っている。口外しない。
cue: You are planning a surprise party for a friend.
reply: Please keep quiet about the party until Saturday.
replyJapanese: 土曜日まで、パーティーのことは黙っていてください。
transferCue: Explain why nobody knew about a colleague's new job.
transferReply: She kept quiet about the offer until she had signed.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は契約書にサインするまで、内定のことを黙っていました。
nuance: The subject follows about. With an object in the middle, keep something quiet means stop other people finding out.
nuanceJapanese: 話題は about で続ける。keep something quiet と目的語をはさむと、「人に知られないようにする」の意味になる。

meaning: Stay with someone so that they are not alone.
japanese: （人の）そばにいてあげる。相手をする。
cue: A friend has a long wait at the hospital.
reply: I'll keep you company until the doctor calls you.
replyJapanese: 先生に呼ばれるまで、一緒にいるよ。
transferCue: Explain why you stayed with your grandmother after her operation.
transferReply: I stayed the weekend to keep her company.
transferReplyJapanese: そばにいてあげようと、週末は泊まりました。
nuance: The person goes in the middle and company takes no article. Do not say keep company to someone.
nuanceJapanese: 人を間に置き、company に冠詞は付かない。keep company to someone とは言わない。

meaning: Used when you need a moment to think.
japanese: ええと。そうですね。
cue: A colleague asks when you are free next week.
reply: Let me see, I could do Tuesday after two.
replyJapanese: ええと、火曜日の2時以降なら大丈夫です。
transferCue: A tourist asks you about the last train.
transferReply: The last train is, let me see, at ten past eleven.
transferReplyJapanese: 最終電車は、ええと、11時10分です。
nuance: A filler that gives you time to think; it does not ask to look at anything. Let's see is used the same way, even when you are alone.
nuanceJapanese: 考える時間をかせぐつなぎ言葉で、何かを見せてほしいという意味ではない。Let's see も、一人のときでも同じように使う。

meaning: Used to say that you have learned something from a surprising or bad experience.
japanese: いい勉強になった。失敗も経験のうちだ。
cue: The wheel of your cheap new suitcase broke on its first trip.
reply: I'll pay a bit more next time. Live and learn.
replyJapanese: 次はもう少しお金を出します。いい勉強になりました。
transferCue: You travelled to a museum and found it closed.
transferReply: I had no idea it shut on Mondays, but you live and learn.
transferReplyJapanese: 月曜休みだとは知りませんでした。まあ、これも勉強ですね。
nuance: Said after a mistake or surprise, usually your own, in a light, accepting tone. British speakers often say you live and learn.
nuanceJapanese: たいてい自分の失敗や驚きのあとに、軽く受け入れる調子で言う。イギリスでは you live and learn の形も多い。

meaning: Stop being patient and start to feel annoyed.
japanese: 我慢できなくなる。しびれを切らす。
cue: The office printer has jammed for the third time today.
reply: I'm starting to lose patience with this printer.
replyJapanese: このプリンターには、そろそろ我慢できなくなってきました。
transferCue: Describe passengers during a long delay.
transferReply: Passengers lost patience when the delay reached two hours.
transferReplyJapanese: 遅れが2時間になると、乗客はしびれを切らしました。
frame: Lose patience with someone or something
nuance: Use with for the person or thing. It is milder than lose your temper, which means actually getting angry.
nuanceJapanese: 相手や対象は with で続ける。実際に怒り出す lose your temper より弱く、いら立ち始める段階を表す。

meaning: Worry about something so much that you cannot sleep.
japanese: （〜を）心配して眠れなくなる。気に病む。
cue: A friend is upset about one poor exam result.
reply: Don't lose sleep over one bad mark.
replyJapanese: 悪い点数1つで、くよくよしないで。
transferCue: Say that a small mistake at work does not worry you.
transferReply: It was a tiny error, and I'm not losing sleep over it.
transferReplyJapanese: ほんの小さなミスですから、気に病んではいません。
nuance: Mostly used in negatives: don't lose sleep over it, I won't lose sleep over that. Sleep takes no article.
nuanceJapanese: don't lose sleep over it、I won't lose sleep over that のように、ほとんど否定文で使う。sleep に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: Stop communicating with someone as time passes.
japanese: 連絡が途絶える。疎遠になる。
cue: Someone asks about your old flatmate.
reply: We lost touch after she moved to Canada.
replyJapanese: 彼女がカナダに引っ越してから、連絡が途絶えました。
transferCue: Say goodbye to a colleague who is leaving the company.
transferReply: Let's not lose touch once you start the new job.
transferReplyJapanese: 新しい仕事が始まっても、連絡を取り合いましょう。
nuance: No article or possessive, and the person follows with. Lose your touch is different: it means no longer do something as well as before.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞も所有格も付けず、相手は with で続ける。lose your touch は「腕が落ちる」という別の意味。

meaning: Go crazy, or start behaving in a very strange way.
japanese: 正気を失う。頭がどうかなる。
cue: Your flatmate wants to swim in the sea in January.
reply: Have you lost your mind? It's minus five outside.
replyJapanese: 正気なの。外はマイナス5度だよ。
transferCue: Describe a week of noisy building work next door.
transferReply: I'll lose my mind if that drilling goes on much longer.
transferReplyJapanese: あのドリルの音がこれ以上続いたら、頭がおかしくなりそうです。
nuance: Informal and usually an exaggeration, not a medical description. The possessive matches the subject: I'm losing my mind, has he lost his mind?
nuanceJapanese: くだけた誇張表現で、医学的な意味ではふつう使わない。所有格は主語に合わせる（I'm losing my mind / Has he lost his mind?）。

meaning: Suddenly become angry.
japanese: かっとなる。怒り出す。
cue: Apologise after shouting at a family member.
reply: I'm sorry I lost my temper with you this morning.
replyJapanese: 今朝は、かっとなってしまってごめんなさい。
transferCue: Describe a calm sports coach.
transferReply: Our coach never loses his temper, even when we play badly.
transferReplyJapanese: 私たちのプレーがひどいときでも、コーチは決してかっとなりません。
nuance: The possessive matches the subject, and the person you are angry with follows with. The opposite is keep your temper.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせ、怒りの相手は with で続ける。反対は keep your temper（怒りを抑える）。

meaning: In a way that is very easy to hear or understand.
japanese: はっきりと。明確に。
cue: Staff complained strongly about a new rota.
reply: The message from the team came through loud and clear.
replyJapanese: チームの言いたいことは、はっきりと伝わってきました。
transferCue: Check the sound at the start of a video call.
transferReply: Yes, I can hear you loud and clear now.
transferReplyJapanese: はい、今ははっきり聞こえています。
frame: Hear / get something loud and clear
nuance: The order is fixed: never clear and loud. It usually follows hear, get or come through, and is often about a message rather than real volume.
nuanceJapanese: 語順は固定で、clear and loud とは言わない。hear、get、come through のあとに置き、実際の音量より、メッセージがはっきり伝わることを言う場合が多い。

meaning: Used to say that people do not see the faults of someone they love.
japanese: 恋は盲目。
cue: Your friend's boyfriend is always late, but she never minds.
reply: She forgives him every time. I suppose love is blind.
replyJapanese: 彼女は毎回彼を許します。恋は盲目ということでしょうね。
transferCue: Laugh about a past relationship of your own.
transferReply: I even liked his terrible singing. Love is blind, they say.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼のひどい歌まで好きでした。恋は盲目と言いますからね。
nuance: A fixed saying with no article, used as a complete comment, often with I suppose or they say. It is gently humorous, not a serious criticism.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞のない決まった言い回しで、I suppose や they say を添え、それだけで一言コメントとして使う。真剣な批判ではなく、軽いユーモアを込めた言い方。

meaning: Make a situation better.
japanese: 状況をよくする。効果がある。
cue: Encourage a friend to start exercising a little.
reply: Even a ten-minute walk each day makes a difference.
replyJapanese: 毎日10分歩くだけでも、違ってきます。
transferCue: Thank volunteers after a charity event.
transferReply: Your help today made a difference to a lot of families.
transferReplyJapanese: 今日の皆さんの手助けは、多くの家族の力になりました。
frame: Make a difference to someone or something
nuance: Add big or real before difference to make it stronger. Make no difference is the opposite: it changes nothing.
nuanceJapanese: difference の前に big や real を入れると強まる。make no difference は反対で、「何も変わらない」の意味。

meaning: Change your expression to show that you do not like something.
japanese: 顔をしかめる。嫌そうな顔をする。
cue: A child tries a new vegetable at dinner.
reply: He made a face when he tasted the spinach.
replyJapanese: 彼はほうれん草を口にして、顔をしかめました。
transferCue: Your partner reacts whenever you talk about your job.
transferReply: Please don't make a face every time I mention work.
transferReplyJapanese: 仕事の話をするたびに、嫌そうな顔をしないでください。
frame: Make a face at someone or something
nuance: British English often says pull a face. Make faces, in the plural, usually means doing funny expressions to make someone laugh.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語では pull a face と言うことが多い。複数形の make faces は、人を笑わせるための変顔を指すことが多い。

meaning: Make someone, often yourself, look silly in front of other people.
japanese: （人を）笑いものにする。恥をかかせる。
cue: Explain why you will not sing at the office party.
reply: I'm not singing. I don't want to make a fool of myself.
replyJapanese: 歌いませんよ。恥をかきたくないので。
transferCue: Complain about a colleague's joke in a meeting.
transferReply: He made a fool of me in front of the whole team.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はチーム全員の前で、私を笑いものにしました。
frame: Make a fool of someone / yourself
nuance: Most common with a reflexive: make a fool of myself, yourself, himself. Keep a before fool and of before the person.
nuanceJapanese: make a fool of myself / yourself / himself のように、再帰代名詞と使うことが最も多い。fool の前の a と、人の前の of を落とさない。

meaning: Earn the money you need to live.
japanese: 生計を立てる。
cue: Someone asks what your brother does.
reply: He makes a living as a wedding photographer.
replyJapanese: 彼は結婚式のカメラマンとして生計を立てています。
transferCue: Talk about how hard a creative career is.
transferReply: It's hard to make a living from painting alone.
transferReplyJapanese: 絵を描くだけで生計を立てるのは難しいです。
frame: Make a living as something / from something
nuance: Use as for the job and from or by for the activity. Earn a living means the same and is slightly more formal.
nuanceJapanese: 職業は as、手段となる活動は from や by で続ける。earn a living も同じ意味で、やや改まった言い方。

meaning: Make a place dirty or untidy.
japanese: 散らかす。汚す。
cue: You come home and find flour all over the kitchen.
reply: The kids made a mess in the kitchen making pancakes.
replyJapanese: 子どもたちがパンケーキを作って、台所を散らかしました。
transferCue: A friend wants to paint a picture in your living room.
transferReply: Paint here if you like, but try not to make a mess.
transferReplyJapanese: ここで描いてもいいけど、汚さないようにね。
nuance: Mess is countable here, so keep a. Make a mess of something has a second meaning: do a task badly.
nuanceJapanese: この mess は可算で、a を落とさない。make a mess of something には「（仕事などを）台なしにする」という別の意味もある。

meaning: Say something that expresses an idea or opinion.
japanese: 意見を述べる。指摘する。
cue: Refer back to a colleague's comment in a meeting.
reply: You made a point earlier about delivery costs.
replyJapanese: 先ほど、配送費について指摘されましたね。
transferCue: Ask to speak before a discussion ends.
transferReply: Can I make a point before we move on?
transferReplyJapanese: 次に進む前に、ひとつ意見を言ってもいいですか。
nuance: The topic follows about. Do not confuse it with make a point of doing something, which means always take care to do it.
nuanceJapanese: 話題は about で続ける。make a point of doing something（必ず〜するようにする）は別の表現なので、混同しないこと。

meaning: Try hard to do something.
japanese: 努力する。がんばって〜しようとする。
cue: Your friend is often late when you meet.
reply: Could you make an effort to be on time tonight?
replyJapanese: 今夜は、時間どおりに来るよう努力してもらえますか。
transferCue: Praise a new neighbour.
transferReply: She has really made an effort to learn everyone's names.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は、みんなの名前を覚えようと本当に努力しています。
frame: Make an effort to do something
nuance: The verb is make, not do, and to plus a verb follows. An adjective goes before effort and an becomes a: make a real effort.
nuanceJapanese: 動詞は do ではなく make で、あとに to + 動詞を続ける。形容詞は effort の前に入り、an は a に変わる（make a real effort）。

meaning: Do something nice for someone because you upset or disappointed them.
japanese: （人に）埋め合わせをする。
cue: You forgot a friend's birthday dinner.
reply: I'm so sorry I missed it. I'll make it up to you.
replyJapanese: 行けなくて本当にごめん。この埋め合わせはするよ。
transferCue: Explain why you are taking your sister to a concert.
transferReply: I cancelled twice, so this is how I'm making it up to her.
transferReplyJapanese: 2回もキャンセルしたので、これで埋め合わせをするつもりです。
nuance: It is fixed and never becomes them, and the person follows to. Make up with someone is different: become friends again after an argument.
nuanceJapanese: it は固定で them などにはならず、相手は to のあとに置く。make up with someone は「仲直りする」で、別の表現。

meaning: Get better at something or get closer to finishing it.
japanese: 進歩する。はかどる。
cue: Your manager asks about a slow project.
reply: We're making progress, but the testing isn't finished yet.
replyJapanese: 進んではいますが、テストはまだ終わっていません。
transferCue: Encourage someone who is learning the piano.
transferReply: You've made progress with your left hand since last month.
transferReplyJapanese: 先月と比べて、左手が上達しましたね。
nuance: Progress is uncountable: no a and no plural. Adjectives go in the middle, as in make good progress or make slow progress.
nuanceJapanese: progress は不可算で、a も複数形も付かない。形容詞は間に入れて、make good progress、make slow progress のように言う。

meaning: Move yourself or other things so that there is space for someone or something.
japanese: 場所を空ける。スペースを作る。
cue: You want to sit with friends on a crowded bench.
reply: Could you move along a bit and make room for me?
replyJapanese: 少し詰めて、私の座る場所を空けてもらえますか。
transferCue: Explain why you sold an old sofa.
transferReply: We sold the sofa to make room for a bigger desk.
transferReplyJapanese: 大きめの机を置く場所を作るために、ソファを売りました。
frame: Make room for someone or something
nuance: Room means space here, so it is uncountable and takes no article: not make a room. Use for before what needs the space.
nuanceJapanese: この room は「空間」の意味で不可算。冠詞は付かず、make a room とは言わない。場所が必要な人や物は for で続ける。

meaning: Be clear and easy to understand.
japanese: 意味が通じる。理解できる。
cue: Ask a colleague to check a report you wrote.
reply: Does the second paragraph make sense to you?
replyJapanese: 2つ目の段落は、意味が通じますか。
transferCue: Describe instructions that confused you at first.
transferReply: The instructions made sense once I looked at the diagram.
transferReplyJapanese: 図を見たら、説明書の内容が理解できました。
nuance: No article before sense, and the thing understood is the subject: it makes sense to me. In make sense of something, the person is the subject.
nuanceJapanese: sense に冠詞は付かず、理解される物事が主語になる（It makes sense to me）。make sense of something は逆に、人が主語になる。

meaning: Use something that is available to you.
japanese: 利用する。活用する。
cue: Give advice to a new student.
reply: You should make use of the free language classes on campus.
replyJapanese: キャンパスの無料の語学クラスを活用するといいですよ。
transferCue: Describe cooking with leftovers.
transferReply: I made use of the leftover rice for today's lunch.
transferReplyJapanese: 残りご飯を、今日の昼食に活用しました。
nuance: Slightly more formal than use, and it suggests taking a chance that is there. Adjectives go before use: make good use of, make full use of.
nuanceJapanese: use よりやや改まった言い方で、せっかくあるものを生かす含みがある。形容詞は use の前に入れる（make good use of、make full use of）。

meaning: Move or travel towards a place.
japanese: （ある場所へ）進む。向かう。
cue: Tell tour members at an airport where to go next.
reply: Please make your way to gate twelve for boarding.
replyJapanese: 搭乗が始まりますので、12番ゲートへお進みください。
transferCue: Describe leaving a crowded festival.
transferReply: We slowly made our way through the crowd to the exit.
transferReplyJapanese: 私たちは人混みの中を、ゆっくり出口へ進みました。
frame: Make your way to / through somewhere
nuance: The possessive matches the subject. It often suggests that the journey takes time or effort, and it sounds polite in announcements.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。時間や手間をかけて進む含みがあり、案内放送ではていねいな言い方として使う。

meaning: Used to say that you will pay for something for another person.
japanese: 私のおごりです。
cue: A friend reaches for the bill after lunch.
reply: Put your wallet away. Lunch is my treat today.
replyJapanese: 財布はしまって。今日のランチは私のおごりだよ。
transferCue: Invite a colleague who helped you yesterday.
transferReply: Come for a coffee after work. It's my treat.
transferReplyJapanese: 仕事のあと、コーヒーに行きましょう。私がごちそうします。
nuance: Friendly and informal; say it's my treat or just my treat. It's on me means the same.
nuanceJapanese: 親しみのあるくだけた言い方で、It's my treat、または My treat だけでも言える。It's on me も同じ意味。

meaning: Used to say that you should not rule something out, because things can change.
japanese: 絶対にないとは言い切れない。
cue: Someone asks if you would ever move abroad.
reply: I can't imagine leaving Osaka, but never say never.
replyJapanese: 大阪を離れるなんて想像できませんが、絶対にないとは言い切れません。
transferCue: A friend says she will never run a marathon.
transferReply: Never say never. You hated swimming once too.
transferReplyJapanese: 絶対ないなんて言わないで。水泳だって昔は嫌いだったでしょう。
nuance: A fixed saying that stands as a complete sentence or follows but. It leaves a door open in a light, often humorous way.
nuanceJapanese: それだけで1文として、または but のあとに置く決まった言い回し。軽く、しばしば冗談めかして可能性を残す。

meaning: Not a serious problem.
japanese: 大したことではない。
cue: A friend apologises for arriving ten minutes late.
reply: It's no big deal. The film hasn't started yet.
replyJapanese: 大したことないよ。映画はまだ始まっていないし。
transferCue: Describe how your manager reacted to a mistake.
transferReply: She treated the missed deadline as no big deal.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は、締め切りに間に合わなかったことを大した問題にしませんでした。
nuance: Informal. Often said to accept an apology or to play down your own help; not a big deal means the same.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた言い方。謝罪を受け流すときや、自分のした手助けを控えめに言うときによく使う。not a big deal も同じ意味。

meaning: Used to say that you think something is very likely.
japanese: きっと。おそらく。
cue: Your sister's flight has just landed.
reply: No doubt she'll call once she has her bags.
replyJapanese: 荷物を受け取ったら、きっと電話してきますよ。
transferCue: Start talking about news that everyone already knows.
transferReply: You've no doubt heard that the office is moving.
transferReplyJapanese: オフィスが移転することは、きっともうお聞きでしょう。
frame: No doubt someone will do something
nuance: On its own it usually means very probably, not complete certainty. For real certainty, say there is no doubt that or without a doubt.
nuanceJapanese: 単独ではふつう「たぶんきっと」程度で、完全な確信ではない。確信を言うなら there is no doubt that や without a doubt を使う。

meaning: Used to say that something surprising is really true.
japanese: 本当に。冗談抜きで。
cue: Tell a friend how long you waited for a table.
reply: No kidding, we queued for two hours outside that café.
replyJapanese: 冗談抜きで、あのカフェの外に2時間並んだんだよ。
transferCue: Insist that a surprising story about a neighbour is true.
transferReply: He cycled here from Kyoto in one day, no kidding.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は京都からここまで、1日で自転車で来たんだ。本当だよ。
nuance: Informal. As a reply, No kidding? shows surprise, and said flatly about something obvious it is sarcastic.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた言い方。相づちの No kidding? は驚きを表し、わかりきったことに平坦な調子で言うと皮肉になる。

meaning: Whatever happens or whatever the result is.
japanese: 何があっても。
cue: Promise to attend a friend's wedding.
reply: I'll be at your wedding in June no matter what.
replyJapanese: 6月の結婚式には、何があっても行くからね。
transferCue: A manager sets a firm deadline.
transferReply: This order has to leave the warehouse today, no matter what.
transferReplyJapanese: この注文品は、何があっても今日中に倉庫から出さなければなりません。
nuance: Here it ends the sentence with nothing after it. It can also start a clause, with a present-tense verb: no matter what happens, not will happen.
nuanceJapanese: この用法では文末に置き、あとに何も続けない。節を導くこともでき、その場合の動詞は現在形にする（no matter what happens。will happen とはしない）。

meaning: Used to say that hearing nothing probably means nothing bad has happened.
japanese: 便りのないのはよい便り。
cue: Your parents worry because your brother has not phoned from his trip.
reply: He hasn't called since Monday, but no news is good news.
replyJapanese: 月曜日から電話がありませんが、便りのないのはよい便りですよ。
transferCue: Calm a colleague who is waiting for a client's reply.
transferReply: They'd tell us if there was a problem. No news is good news.
transferReplyJapanese: 問題があれば知らせてくるはずです。便りのないのはよい便りですよ。
nuance: News is uncountable, so the verb is is, never are. Said to calm someone who is waiting to hear.
nuanceJapanese: news は不可算なので、動詞は is で、are にはしない。連絡を待って心配している人を落ち着かせるために言う。

meaning: Used to say that you must work hard or suffer a little to improve.
japanese: 苦労なくして得るものなし。
cue: Your legs ache after a hard training session.
reply: My legs really hurt today, but no pain no gain.
replyJapanese: 今日は脚がかなり痛いですが、苦労なくして得るものなしです。
transferCue: A friend finds daily piano practice boring.
transferReply: Keep doing your scales every day. No pain no gain.
transferReplyJapanese: 音階の練習は毎日続けて。苦労なくして得るものなしだよ。
nuance: Usually written with a comma: no pain, no gain. Common in sport and study, and often said with a smile rather than as serious advice.
nuanceJapanese: 書くときはふつうコンマを入れて no pain, no gain とする。スポーツや勉強の場面でよく使い、真剣な助言というより、笑顔で軽く言うことが多い。

meaning: Not useful, or not likely to succeed.
japanese: 役に立たない。（〜しても）無駄だ。
cue: A friend keeps phoning someone whose phone is switched off.
reply: It's no use calling him. His phone is off.
replyJapanese: 彼に電話しても無駄だよ。電源が切れているから。
transferCue: Explain why you threw away an old map.
transferReply: The map was no use because half the roads had changed.
transferReplyJapanese: 道の半分が変わっていて、その地図は役に立ちませんでした。
nuance: After it's no use, the verb takes -ing: it's no use waiting, not to wait. Be of no use is a more formal form.
nuanceJapanese: it's no use のあとの動詞は -ing 形にする（it's no use waiting。to wait にはしない）。be of no use はより改まった形。

meaning: Used to say that something is not completely true or correct.
japanese: そういうわけでもない。正確には違う。
cue: A colleague thinks you have agreed to lead a project.
reply: Not exactly. I said I'd think about it.
replyJapanese: そういうわけではありません。考えてみると言ったんです。
transferCue: A friend repeats a message wrongly.
transferReply: That's not exactly what the email said.
transferReplyJapanese: メールに書いてあったのは、正確にはそうではありません。
nuance: A soft way to correct someone, gentler than no. Before an adjective it can be ironic: it's not exactly cheap means it is expensive.
nuanceJapanese: 相手をやんわり訂正する言い方で、no より柔らかい。形容詞の前では皮肉にもなり、It's not exactly cheap は「高い」の意味。

meaning: Used to say that you are not completely sure about something.
japanese: 完全には〜ない。はっきりとは〜ない。
cue: A friend asks what time the film starts.
reply: I'm not quite sure, so let me check the website.
replyJapanese: はっきりとはわからないので、サイトを確認してみます。
transferCue: Colleagues ask about a change of manager.
transferReply: It's still not quite clear who will lead the team.
transferReplyJapanese: 誰がチームを率いるのかは、まだはっきりしていません。
nuance: Softer and more polite than not sure. With a verb, quite follows the negative: I don't quite understand, I didn't quite catch that.
nuanceJapanese: not sure より柔らかく、ていねいに響く。動詞と使うときは、否定語のあとに quite を置く（I don't quite understand / I didn't quite catch that）。

meaning: Used to say that it is hard to stop doing something you have done for a long time.
japanese: 長年の習慣は、なかなか抜けない。
cue: You have retired but still get up early.
reply: I retired last year but still wake at six. Old habits die hard.
replyJapanese: 去年退職したのに、今も6時に目が覚めます。長年の習慣は抜けないものです。
transferCue: A colleague still prints every email.
transferReply: He prints every email, so I guess old habits die hard.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はメールを全部印刷しています。長年の習慣は、なかなか抜けないんでしょうね。
nuance: A fixed saying: habits is plural and hard never becomes hardly. Used as a mild excuse or gentle joke, not for serious problems.
nuanceJapanese: 決まった言い回しで、habits は複数形、hard を hardly にはしない。軽い言い訳や冗談として使い、深刻な問題には使わない。

meaning: Eating less, or only certain foods, usually to lose weight.
japanese: ダイエット中である。食事制限をしている。
cue: A colleague offers you a slice of cake.
reply: It looks lovely, but I'm on a diet this month.
replyJapanese: おいしそうですが、今月はダイエット中なんです。
transferCue: Talk about your father's health.
transferReply: My father went on a diet after his check-up in spring.
transferReplyJapanese: 父は春の健康診断のあと、食事制限を始めました。
frame: Be on a diet / go on a diet
nuance: Be on a diet is the state; go on a diet means start one. It is about food only, not exercise.
nuanceJapanese: be on a diet は状態、go on a diet は始めること。日本語の「ダイエット」と違い、運動は含まず、食事の制限だけを指す。

meaning: Continuing for a long time without stopping.
japanese: 延々と。長々と。
cue: Describe a boring speech at a ceremony.
reply: The speech went on and on for nearly an hour.
replyJapanese: スピーチは1時間近く、延々と続きました。
transferCue: Complain about a neighbour who loves his new car.
transferReply: He talks on and on about his new car.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は新しい車のことを、延々と話し続けます。
nuance: It follows a verb such as go, talk or drive, and usually sounds bored or annoyed. Go on and on about something means keep talking about it.
nuanceJapanese: go、talk、drive などの動詞のあとに置き、たいてい退屈やうんざりした気持ちがこもる。go on and on about something は「〜について延々と話す」。
